change.author: Sam Jewell

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: Both branches return false (`if enabled { return false }; return false`), and `enabled` holds the negated flag, so the name and variable contradict the result. The `sqlExpressions` toggle (registry.go:1083, "Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions.") is now a no-op: turning it on still gives a hard error. If the goal is to disable the feature unconditionally, replace the helper with a plain early return and a comment. If it is meant to be re-enabled later, write `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and let the stub in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` fail. The error text "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is also misleading when the flag is on. The toggle's description is now stale too.

findings.title: Legacy node path is disabled only by the stub, with a misleading error
findings.body: The reader.go guard covers only the `ExpressionQueryReader` path, which `nodes.go:123` uses only when the `FlagExpressionParser` toggle is on. With the parser toggle off, `nodes.go:159-160` calls `UnmarshalSQLCommand`, then `NewSQLCommand`, then `sql.TablesList`. That reaches the stub `RunCommands`, which returns "not implemented". `NewSQLCommand` turns it into a BadRequest with the public message "error reading SQL command" (lines 30-36). The result is the same for the user (SQL expressions don't work), but the message blames their SQL instead of saying the feature is disabled. A single check at `NewSQLCommand` would cover both paths and give one clear message.

contracts.action: SQL-type expression query is read via ExpressionQueryReader
contracts.equivalent_path: Threshold case at pkg/expr/reader.go:160 gates RecoveryThreshold with h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)
contracts.before_after: The threshold path reads the real flag value. The new SQL path calls enableSqlExpressions, which always returns false, so it returns the error before ReadVal runs whatever the flag says.
contracts.visible_effect: The caller of ReadQuery gets "sqlExpressions is not implemented" for every SQL query.
contracts.failure_mode: Not applicable. This is a synchronous error return with no state kept. Enabling the toggle has no effect.

contracts.action: SQLCommand/TablesList now use the stub sql.DB instead of go-duck
contracts.equivalent_path: Legacy node path pkg/expr/nodes.go:159-160 (UnmarshalSQLCommand -> NewSQLCommand -> sql.TablesList)
contracts.before_after: Before, go-duck ran DuckDB. Now TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto always return errors.New("not implemented"). NewSQLCommand maps the TablesList error to a BadRequest with a generic message. Execute returns rsp.Error with a nil error.
contracts.visible_effect: Creating an SQL expression fails with "error reading SQL command". Execute, if it were ever reached, would put the "not implemented" error in the result.
contracts.failure_mode: The failure is visible to the user as an error, not silent. No state is left behind. Nothing else in the repo imports go-duck or the removed indirect modules, so the go.mod and go.sum removals are consistent.

summary: The PR removes go-duck and replaces it with a stub `sql.DB` whose methods always return \"not implemented\". It also adds a feature guard in `reader.go` that always rejects SQL queries. The dependency removals look consistent: I found no remaining imports of the removed modules. Both findings are minor. `enableSqlExpressions` has self-contradicting logic and ignores the toggle, and the legacy node path is disabled only by the stub, with a misleading \"error reading SQL command\" message.
